gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patients with histologically confirmed glioblastoma, recurrent after prior radiotherapy and temozolomide chemotherapy.

candidate_evidence.quote: Efficacy and Safety of NaviFUS System add-on Bevacizumab (BEV) in Recurrent GBM Patients
The BEV is the best physician's choice of standard of care for rGBM after prior radiotherapy and temozolomide chemotherapy in the LinKou Chang Gung Memorial Hospital.

candidate_flag.reason: Bevacizumab is an established GBM therapy (rule 6) but its FUS-enabled delivery is the question (C12/R5 could make it a device-dependent candidate).

role_evidence.quote: to investigate the efficacy and safety of FUS add-on bevacizumab (BEV) in rGBM patients

flag.reason: Established GBM therapy given with FUS-mediated BBB opening; if C12/R5 overrides rule 6 it would be a candidate (experimental_monotherapy, device_dependent true).

role_evidence.quote: patients will receive microbubbles (MB) (SonoVue®) 0.1 mL/kg and optimal ultrasound exposure doses (based on the acoustic emission feedback FUS power control algorithm) generated from the NaviFUS System single exposure unit for up to two minutes every 2 weeks to transiently open the BBB.

agents.drug_class_hint: ultrasound contrast agent microbubbles (sulfur hexafluoride) used with focused ultrasound for BBB opening

coder_notes: Registered phase NA (device pilot). Only drug is bevacizumab (standard of care, established GBM therapy per D6) given with NaviFUS focused-ultrasound BBB opening using SonoVue microbubbles. Coded bevacizumab as established_therapy_experiment (rule 6 exception (i)) rather than a device-dependent candidate; flagged uncertain for adjudication. If treated as candidate: role experimental_monotherapy, device_dependent true, regimen monotherapy, has_eligible_candidate true. SonoVue is not a separate registered intervention but is described in the arm and in the NaviFUS device intervention. Degree of BBB opening on DCE-MRI is a device endpoint, not candidate target engagement.
